content.title: About
content.content: Eggnog is a traditional festive drink made from eggs, milk, sugar and spirits (usually rum, brandy or whiskey). It has a thick, creamy texture, a sweet‑spicy flavor with hints of vanilla, and the alcohol gives it a warming effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggnog originated in medieval England as a "egg punch" and was originally non‑alcoholic.
In the United States the drink became popular during the colonial era, when Caribbean rum was added.
Typical spices for eggnog are cinnamon, nutmeg and clove.
In some regions eggnog is served cold, in others hot, depending on climate and tradition.
There is a non‑alcoholic version often served to children and those who abstain from spirits.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Milk and cream supply calcium and vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and dairy contain riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Nutmeg and cinnamon are rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Egg or dairy allergy
items.content: Eggnog can trigger allergic reactions in people sensitive to eggs or milk.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Traditional recipes contain a lot of sugar, which may contribute to weight gain and blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Alcohol intoxication
items.content: Excessive consumption of alcoholic eggnog can lead to intoxication and associated hazards.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: If made with raw eggs and not kept properly chilled, there is a risk of salmonella infection.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve eggnog in small glasses or mugs, often topped with whipped cream and a pinch of nutmeg. It can be enjoyed hot in cold weather or chilled in warm weather. Additional spirits (rum, brandy) may be added to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared eggnog should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 3‑4 days. For longer storage, portion it into sealed containers to prevent oxidation and bacterial growth.
